speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Specifically, Article 51(6) of the Constitution provides that the terms of service of the staff of Parliament may be determined by Parliament after receiving the advice of a Commission consisting of the following persons, either Speaker as Chairman, not more than three Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister and a member of the Public Service Commission.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This Commission comprised: yourself, Mr Speaker; the Minister for National Development, Mr Chee Hong Tat; the Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance, Mr Jeffrey Siow; Mr Ramli Buang, a member of the Public Service Commission; and myself.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Commission presented its Report to Parliament on 27 July 2026.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The staff of Parliament comprise the Clerk of Parliament and the officers who assist him, such as Parliamentary Clerks; and Language Service Officers who are on the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and the Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008), respectively.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since 2008, these schemes have adopted a salary and performance-based framework similar to the Management Executive Scheme (2008) in the Civil Service.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On 20 February 2026, the Public Service Division (PSD) announced that eligible civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008) would receive salary adjustments of 2% to 9% to keep pace with market standards and enable the Public Service to continue to attract and retain talent to deliver well for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These adjustments took effect on 1 August 2026.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will bring these schemes in line with the current framework for the wider Civil Service and supports the continued attraction and retention of officers in the Parliamentary Service.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Commission also recommends introducing a retention payment component for Parliamentary Clerks under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008), and for this to take effect from 1 September 2026.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The volume of parliamentary work has increased substantially over the years.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Further, our Parliamentary Clerks handle increasingly complex and novel questions of parliamentary business and rules.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As the pool of Parliamentary Clerks is small, each departure has a disproportionate impact on the operational effectiveness of the Parliament Secretariat.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The work of Parliamentary Clerks is highly specialised.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are challenges recruiting suitable candidates, especially qualified legal professionals.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even where suitable officers are recruited, time is needed for the officers to acquire the proficiency needed for such work.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Commission's recommendations are aimed at ensuring that the terms of service of the staff of Parliament remain competitive in attracting and retaining strong officers in the schemes of service of the Parliamentary Service.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This Motion may appear administrative, but at its heart, it speaks to something very important: making sure that the staff who support Parliament every day have fair, updated and sustainable terms of service.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The Commission's first recommendation is to align the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and the Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) with the recent adjustments to the Management Executive Scheme (2008).

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Since our Parliament staff have followed the Management Executive Scheme framework since 2008, it is only right and fair that they receive the same adjustments.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The second recommendation introducing a retention payment component for Parliamentary Clerks is especially important.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Parliamentary Clerks form a small group of specialists, their work is highly technical, demanding and central to the smooth running of our Sittings, committees and legislative processes.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Major Bills today routinely involve extensive clause by clause scrutiny and complex amendments.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Recent examples include the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Bill and the Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill which introduced new regulatory duties for digital platforms and critical infrastructures with technical definitions and multi-agency coordination that our clerks must manage with precision.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Committee work has also grown more demanding in the last few years.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The Public Petitions Committee has handled increasingly complex petitions such as the 2023 petition on the Maintenance of Parents Act, which required hearings, legal analysis and a detailed report.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Earlier petitions on housing policies for single unwed parents and on strengthening of harassment protection also involve substantial stakeholder engagement and cross agency coordination.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: On top of this, our Sittings now regularly see over a hundred Parliamentary Questions filed.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Members are seeking clarifications on complex policy areas such as digital regulations, sustainability and cost of living measures.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: All these developments place heavier demands on our Clerks, who must manage complex procedures, tighter timelines and a broader range of legislative issues than ever before.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Recruitment has also become more challenging, especially for legally trained officers who can handle the specialised nature of Parliamentary work.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And when good officers join us, the training required to reach proficiency is extensive.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As the report states, there is also substantial replacement costs and a clear need to retain officers long enough to build up the specialised competencies Parliament relies on.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This is a sensible and targeted measure to strengthen retention, reduce turnover and ensure that Parliament continues to have a stable, experienced secretariat.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It is an investment in institutional capability, one that ultimately supports the functioning of this House and the quality of our legislative work.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The Commission has considered the matter carefully and PSD has also supported the proposals.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: These recommendations are measured, justified and aligned with the long-term needs of Parliament.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Most importantly, they recognise the contributions of our Clerks and secretariat officers, whose work is often behind the scenes but absolutely essential to the smooth running of this House.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Accepting these recommendations is an investment in Parliament's capability.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It strengthens Parliament's capacity to scrutinise, legislate and engage the public with continuity and professionalism.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For these reasons, Mr Speaker, I support the Motion.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I think we ought to start by recognising the critical work that our Parliamentary Clerks, staff and translators carry out behind the scenes to ensure that Parliamentary business, which is very serious business, runs smoothly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They support the Office of the Speaker, Members of this House and Select Committees in the proper conduct of Parliamentary business.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They advice on Parliamentary procedure and examine Parliamentary Questions, Motions, amendments and other papers to ensure compliance with the Constitution, Standing Orders and established practices.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They also support Sittings and committee proceedings, and maintain authoritative Parliament records, or Hansard.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In other words, their work, often unseen, helps ensure that our Parliament can make decisions for Singapore smoothly, efficiently and effectively.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We should therefore recognise them for their integrity and ever reliability, and for their ability to think on their feet when applying the Standing Orders objectively and professionally.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They do all this while Sittings happen in public view and scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, right in front of the cameras that are rolling live even now.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And the need for accuracy and adherence to our Standing Orders is paramount for public accountability and transparency.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because what we debate here could well become law, because national policies are fine-tuned in this House, I think we ought to take a moment to credit our Parliament Clerks, secretariat, staff and the translators for all their hard work.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can I invite the House to record our support for them?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In short, the professional support needed to ensure robustness of debate and accuracy of policy is extremely important.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Hence, I firmly believe it is important to recognise the significance of the duties Parliamentary staff carry out for all Members of the House, be they Government Members of Parliament or Opposition backbenchers, elected, or Non-Constituency Members of Parliament (NCMPs) or Nominated Members of Parliament (NMPs).

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, I know that our Parliamentary secretariat has seen the evolution of Singapore's Parliament from being a fully elected house to one with NCMPs and NMPs, so we should recognise the accuracy and professionalism of our clerks and all the staff.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Once we agree in principle, with the recognition of our Parliamentary staff, I think the natural corollary or the practical consideration which follows is that remuneration should match the significance of their work.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These adjustments are much needed, and I am in full support.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I note that the last review was some time ago, in fact, many years ago.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, compared to salaries being paid in the private sector – and I have no doubt the capability of our Parliamentary staff can match those of people in the private sector – it has actually been behind the curve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In this regard, I think it is fair that the changes will be on par with those, or broadly on par with those on the Civil Service.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I might even go so far to urge that when we consider the importance of Parliament in keeping Singapore viable and adaptable in today's competitive and changing world, the remuneration of our Parliamentary staff should in fact be at the forefront of the curve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I am therefore happy and much encouraged that Mr Speaker has personally taken this proposal up.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, Sir, I recall my conversation with you together with then Deputy Speaker Jessica Tan, where we raised some years ago, the need to raise salaries for our Parliamentary staff.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I therefore wish to put on record my thanks to you, Mr Speaker, Sir, for your leadership and for taking this up.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The question here is how do we ensure that recognition, when matched with remuneration, will result in a responsible officer.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To this, I say there is no doubt in my mind that the ethos of responsibility runs deep within our Parliamentary Clerks, secretariat, translators and staff.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To this we need not look any further than the four to five unprecedented Budgets we passed in 2020 when Singapore was in the throes of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As a House, we decided to meet in person, physically, no such thing as Zoom parliaments in this jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We therefore passed the Budgets, ensuring safety and viability, while ensuring safe distancing within the House.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I remember those days and some of us who have been in this Chamber long enough remember those days.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Masks on, empty seats between each Member, but the House was filled, nevertheless.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Through it all, our Parliament staff worked hard to ensure that Parliamentary business continued in the depths of the crisis.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And holding up that placard and counting every single Member was important because we needed a certain amount of super majority vote to use our reserves.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In this, I saw great resilience and how in this House we have an institution where people are committed to a cause bigger than themselves.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is why I am confident these responsibilities will be carried out by our professional Parliament staff.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I do not want to be presumptuous, but any clarifications for the Leader?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am quite sure with it, they will help me and help us do our job better.
